subject: Renewal architecture: surge guardrail + smoothing proposal
messages:
From: Oliver Park <oliver.park@brightcore.io>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Jul 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning: surge risk & term structure

Logan —

Thanks for the partnership this year. We're heading into budgeting for FY29 and want to lock a renewal before the end of August. A few constraints on our side:

- We want a multi-year relationship (2–3 years) but need flexibility for quarter-to-quarter spikes — Q4 historically has unpredictable batch runs.
- Auto-renew is OK provided there's a clear churn/cancellation window and a predictable true-up.
- We prefer co-terming across multiple Redwood products to simplify procurement.

Can you outline a concrete structure that:
1) gives Brightcore a baseline committed volume with a reasonable uplift path (staged ramp),
2) offers a safe way to handle surges (canary/burst allowance or temporary overage cap) without immediate punitive overage invoicing, and
3) preserves the option to auto-renew but with a 60-day opt-out notice?

Attached is our Q2 usage export so you can see burst patterns. Happy to jump on a 30-min call this week — Rachel (cc) manages procurement and will coordinate the legal/PO side.

Thanks,
Oliver
Director of Platform Engineering
Brightcore Labs

Attachment: Brightcore_usage_Q2.csv (CSV, 45 KB)

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Park <oliver.park@brightcore.io>
Cc: Rachel Lin <rachel.lin@brightcore.io>
Date: Tue, 18 Jul 2028 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning: surge risk & term structure

Oliver — great to see the usage export, thanks. High level answer up front: we can structure a hybrid multi‑year agreement that balances predictability and surge safety without removing your flexibility. Below is a concise proposal so you can take it to procurement/legal.

Proposal (summary):
- Term: 36 months with annual billing cadence and an early-exit true-up window. Co-terming across our API and Dedicated pools is supported.
- Baseline commit: Year 1 = 60% of last 12‑month run‑rate (staged quarterly ramp to full baseline by Q2 year 1). Years 2–3: baseline increases by agreed uplift percentages (optional addendum).
- Canary burst allowance: 60-day rolling canary window for sudden high-tail usage. During the first 60 days of any unexpected surge we provide a 1) temporary uplift buffer = up to 40% of baseline, and 2) invoice smoothing where overage is billed but eligible for credits applied over the next 3 invoices if usage normalizes.
- True-up & smoothing: monthly usage true-up; overages above the canary buffer are billed at overage rates but subject to a smoothing credit schedule if usage returns to baseline within 90 days.
- Auto-renew: 30‑day advance notice to elect not to renew; procurement can lock in 60‑day opt‑out if we include an auto‑renew exemption clause in SOW.
- Pricing: propose a blended discount of 18% on committed tokens for Year 1, step down to 12% Year 2, 8% Year 3 (we can finalize in collaboration with your finance team).

I've attached a light SOW draft (RDW_SOW_hybrid_commit_v0.1.pdf) that codifies the canary window and smoothing credits. Would you and Rachel be available Thursday 11:00–11:30 PT for a quick alignment? If that works I'll loop in Karthik and Marissa for pricing sign-off.

Best,
Logan Wright
Senior Account Executive — Renewals & Expansion
Redwood Inference

Attachment: RDW_SOW_hybrid_commit_v0.1.pdf (PDF, 12 pages)

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Jul 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: INTERNAL: Brightcore renewal — approve canary buffer & discount cadence

Karthik / Marissa —

Quick summary: Brightcore (RDW-2028-3421) wants a 36‑month hybrid commit with staged ramp and a 60‑day canary burst allowance. I proposed the following commercially:
- Canary allowance: temporary buffer up to +40% of baseline for the first 60 days of a detected surge. Overages during the buffer are billed but eligible for credits applied over the next 3 invoices if usage returns to baseline.
- Monthly true-up, with smoothing credits if usage normalizes within 90 days.
- Discount cadence: Y1 18% / Y2 12% / Y3 8% off list for committed token usage.

Questions for you:
1) Approve the 40% / 60‑day buffer language from an risk perspective? We expect this to be used primarily by their batch Q4 runs.
2) Any objections to spreading usage credits over 3 invoices instead of a single credit? Finance (Ben) — does that create recognition or billing friction?
3) Should we require a minimum notice to trigger a planned burst (they can request scheduled bursts in addition to the automatic canary)? I'm leaning to allow scheduled burst requests with 7 business days notice and no credit needed (billed at agreed burst rates).

I need a quick thumbs-up so I can lock the Thursday 11:00 call with Brightcore and present a final SOW.

Thanks —
Logan
Senior Account Executive

Logan / team —

Thanks for the clear proposal and the SOW draft. The structure looks sane and addresses our top concerns. A couple of quick asks before we kick procurement: 

- Can we set the canary buffer at 50% instead of 40% for Q4 only (we can make that a calendar‑driven addendum)?
- Please include the 60‑day opt‑out language in the SOW (we can agree to 30 days for renewals after year 1).
- Rachel, can you confirm procurement will accept monthly true-ups and smoothing credits over 3 invoices?

If Redwood can accept the Q4 50% temporary uplift (calendar addendum) we can route the SOW through DocuSign next week. I cc'd Legal to speed the review.

Oliver
